passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations is based upon, and should be read in conjunction with, our audited consolidated financial statements and the related notes included in this annual report. This report contains forward-looking statements. See “Forward-Looking Information.” In evaluating our business, you should carefully consider the information provided under the caption “Item 3.D. Key Information—Risk Factors” in this annual report. We caution you that our businesses and financial performance are subject to substantial risks and uncertainties. A. Operating Results Overview We are a leading supply chain-based technology and service provider. Our e-commerce business includes online retail and online marketplace. In the online retail business, we acquire products from suppliers and sell them directly to our customers primarily through our mobile apps and websites. In the online marketplace business, third-party merchants sell products to customers primarily through our mobile apps and websites. We also offer marketing, logistics and other value-added services. 133 Table of Contents We generated total net revenues of RMB1,084.7 billion, RMB1,158.8 billion and RMB1,309.1 billion (US$187.2 billion) in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Our online retail business generated net product revenues of RMB871.2 billion, RMB928.0 billion and RMB1,023.8 billion (US$146.4 billion) in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. In addition, our marketplace and marketing, logistics and other services generated net service revenues of RMB213.4 billion, RMB230.8 billion and RMB285.3 billion (US$40.8 billion) in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Due to the PRC legal restrictions on foreign ownership of companies that engage in a value-added telecommunications service business and certain other businesses in China, we conduct the relevant parts of our operations through consolidated variable interest entities. We have contractual arrangements with these entities and their shareholders that enable us to effectively control and receive substantially all of the economic benefits from the entities. Accordingly, we consolidate the results of these entities in our financial statements. Major Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations Our results of operations and financial condition are affected by the general factors driving China’s retail industry, including levels of per capita disposable income and consumer spending in China. In addition, they are also affected by factors driving online retail in China, such as the growing number of online shoppers, the adoption of online sales strategies by manufacturers and service providers, the availability of improved delivery services and the increasing variety of payment options. Our results of operations are also affected by general economic conditions in China. In particular, we have experienced and expect to continue to experience upward pressure on our operating expenses. Our results of operations are also affected by PRC regulations and industry policies related to our business operations, licenses and permits and corporate structure. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Risks Related to Our Business If we are unable to manage our growth or execute our strategies effectively, our business and prospects may be materially and adversely affected. Our business has continued to grow in recent years, and we expect continued growth in our business and revenues. We plan to further invest in technologies, expand our fulfillment infrastructure and increase our product and service offerings. For example, in 2025, we recruited new employees in connection with the expansion of our fulfillment infrastructure and strengthening of our supply chain-based technology and service capability. We will continue to invest resources in training, managing and motivating our workforce. We also plan to continue to build our warehouses and establish new fulfillment facilities in additional locations across China, including smaller, less developed areas. In addition, as we continue to increase our product and service offerings, we will need to work with a large number of new suppliers and third-party merchants efficiently and establish and maintain mutually beneficial relationships with our existing and new suppliers and third-party merchants. To support our growth, we also plan to implement a variety of new and upgraded managerial, operating, financial and human resource systems, procedures and controls. All these efforts will require significant managerial, financial and human resources. We cannot assure you that we will be able to effectively manage our growth or to implement all these systems, procedures and control measures successfully or that our new business initiatives will be successful. If we are not able to manage our growth or execute our strategies effectively, our expansion may not be successful and our business and prospects may be materially and adversely affected. 23 Table of Contents If we are unable to provide superior customer experience, our business and reputation may be materially and adversely affected. The success of our business hinges on our ability to provide superior customer experience, which in turn depends on a variety of factors. These factors include our ability to continue to offer authentic products at competitive prices, source products to respond to customer demands, maintain the quality of our products and services, attract and regulate third-party merchants on our online marketplace, and provide timely and reliable delivery, flexible payment options and superior after-sales service. We rely primarily on our own fulfillment infrastructure, and to a lesser extent on third-party couriers, to deliver our products. Interruptions or failures in our delivery services or third-party couriers could prevent the timely or successful delivery of our products. These interruptions may be due to unforeseen events that are beyond our control or the control of our third-party couriers, such as inclement weather, natural disasters, virus outbreaks, transportation disruptions or labor unrest. If our products are not delivered on time or are delivered in a damaged state, customers may refuse to accept our products and have less confidence in our services. credit_strengths.text: JD's balance sheet carries a substantial net cash position, with cash and short-term investments exceeding reported borrowings by a wide margin. This liquidity buffer materially reduces refinancing risk and provides capacity to absorb working-capital swings in the retail cycle. The indicative financial risk profile is Minimal, reflecting that cash resources comfortably cover the debt stack.

Operating cash flow remains solidly positive and covers capital expenditure, leaving free cash flow available for shareholder returns and investment. The scale of internally generated funds supports the view that JD can fund its fulfillment and technology build-out without incremental leverage, even as operating income compressed sharply in the latest fiscal year.

key_risks.text: Operating income fell sharply in the latest fiscal year, and the operating margin is now a fraction of the sector median. This compression reflects heavy investment in fulfillment infrastructure, new employees and supply-chain technology, as disclosed in the risk factors. If these growth investments do not translate into revenue efficiency, profitability could remain under pressure.

Interest coverage is thin, with operating income barely covering gross interest expense. The debt stack includes both long-term borrowings with current maturities and separately tagged short-term borrowings, so refinancing concentration is a live consideration. A sustained earnings downturn would quickly erode the already narrow coverage cushion.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt sits in line with the sector median, indicating that internally generated cash can service borrowings at a pace comparable to peers. However, the ratio is not high in absolute terms, and the sharp decline in operating cash flow from prior years warrants monitoring for any further deterioration.

The current ratio is marginally below the sector median, and the working-capital position is tight relative to the scale of current liabilities. With a large portion of debt in short-term borrowings, JD relies on continuous access to refinancing. The net cash position mitigates this, but the liquidity profile is not as comfortable as headline cash suggests.

overall_credit_view.text: JD's credit profile is anchored by a net cash balance sheet and substantial operating cash flow, which together support a Minimal indicative financial risk profile. The company's scale in China's retail and supply-chain technology sector provides revenue diversity, but profitability has weakened materially, and interest coverage is thin relative to sector medians.

Our forward-looking view is that JD can manage its debt obligations given the cash buffer, but the combination of compressed margins, heavy investment spending and shareholder distributions that absorb most free cash flow leaves limited headroom. We would monitor operating income recovery and refinancing of short-term borrowings as key credit drivers.

credit_strengths.text: 京東的資產負債表持有可觀的淨現金狀況，現金及短期投資大幅超過所呈報的借款。此流動性緩衝顯著降低再融資風險，並提供能力吸收零售週期中的營運資金波動。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，反映現金資源穩健覆蓋債務結構。
營運現金流保持穩健正值並覆蓋資本開支，留下自由現金流可用於股東回報及投資。內部產生資金的規模支持京東可在不增加槓桿的情況下為其履約及技術建設提供資金，即使營運收入於最近財政年度大幅壓縮。

key_risks.text: 營運收入於最近財政年度大幅下降，而營運利潤率現僅為行業中位數的一小部分。此壓縮反映對履約基礎設施、新員工及供應鏈技術的沉重投資，如風險因素所披露。若該等增長投資未能轉化為收入效率，盈利能力可能持續受壓。
利息覆蓋率偏薄，營運收入僅勉強覆蓋總利息支出。債務結構包括長期借款及流動到期部分，以及另行標示的短期借款，因此再融資集中度為一項現實考量。若盈利持續下滑，將迅速侵蝕本已狹窄的覆蓋緩衝。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率與行業中位數一致，表明內部產生現金可按與同業相若的速度償付借款。然而，該比率絕對水平並不高，且營運現金流較往年大幅下降，值得監察任何進一步惡化。
流動比率略低於行業中位數，且營運資金狀況相對於流動負債規模偏緊。由於大部分債務為短期借款，京東依賴持續的再融資渠道。淨現金狀況緩解此情況，但流動性狀況不如表面現金所示般寬裕。

overall_credit_view.text: 京東的信用狀況以淨現金資產負債表及可觀營運現金流為錨，兩者共同支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。該公司在中國零售及供應鏈技術行業的規模提供收入多元化，但盈利能力已大幅減弱，且利息覆蓋率相對於行業中位數偏薄。
我們的前瞻性觀點是，京東憑藉現金緩衝可管理其債務責任，但利潤率壓縮、沉重投資開支及吸收大部分自由現金流的股東分派相結合，留下有限空間。我們將監察營運收入復甦及短期借款再融資作為關鍵信用驅動因素。
